title: Vacuum Toilet Assembly Change on Withdrawal of the Original Supplier
abstract: Introduction of a replacement vacuum toilet assembly on aircraft carrying the original supplier standard, after that supplier left the aerospace market and its repair network closed.

sections.reason: The original vacuum toilet supplier exited the aerospace market in 2021 and its authorised repair network closed within a year. Twelve aircraft in the fleet still carried that standard, and the operators concerned were already cannibalising retired aircraft for flush valves and rinse rings. A toilet out of service is not an airworthiness matter but it is a dispatch and passenger experience matter on an aircraft that carries this many people, and two operators had begun placarding units off on long sectors.
sections.description: The bowl, the flush valve and the rinse ring are replaced by the assembly already fitted to later aircraft, using an adapter frame so that the existing monument cut-out is not changed. The lower latch assembly D3830119707579 is replaced by the item used on the later standard, and plain washers EN887884-5C are used at the adapter frame interface. The waste disposal galley insert kit XAN707755-87 is refitted unchanged. The obsolete spacer LN562957-2B is deleted at the drain line clamp, which now uses a bonded support. The panel at FIN 869WP is renewed because the later bowl sits 12 mm further aft, and the seat track cover at FIN 2625WP is disturbed for access to the drain run. Work is in zones 122, 191, 941 and 943. Revised detail is on drawing D38300073011.
sections.effects: Mass increase of 3.2 kg per unit, and on a full aircraft installation of sixteen units that is 51 kg distributed along the cabin. No electrical load change; the flush cycle draws the same current from the same busbar. The replacement assembly is not interchangeable with the original because the adapter frame is required, but once the frame is fitted the unit is a line-replaceable item. Servicing and drain line flushing content requires update, and the illustrated parts content for the toilet assembly is re-issued in full.
sections.embodiment_note: Retrofit only, on the twelve aircraft still at the original standard. Embodiment is a base task of about six days for a full aircraft, or unit by unit at any base visit since each toilet is independent. Kits are supplied per unit with the adapter frame included.

type_data.balance_impact: Distributed along the cabin, CG shift below 0.02 % MAC
type_data.production_impact: No production cut-in; the later standard was already the build standard

This is a scheduling note passed to planning, not an engineering condition; neither change depends on the other and either may be embodied alone.
